title: USCIS Confirms FY2027 H-1B Cap Reached, No Second Lottery as Wage-Weighted System Reshapes Selection
excerpt: The first year of wage-based H-1B selection saw registrations drop 38% while heavily favoring higher-paid positions, leaving thousands of Indian tech workers without a path forward until spring 2027.
body:
• USCIS received enough petitions to fill all 85,000 FY2027 H-1B slots — 65,000 regular cap and 20,000 master's exemption — and will not conduct a second lottery.
  • Unique registrations fell 38.5% to 211,600, down from 336,153 in FY2026, in the first year of the wage-weighted selection system.
  • 71.5% of selected beneficiaries held U.S. advanced degrees, up from 57% last year, with only 17.7% selected from the lowest wage category.
  • Unselected registrations cannot carry forward; the next opportunity opens in spring 2027 for FY2028.

Cap Closed After Single Lottery Round

U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services announced on July 17, 2026, that it has received enough H-1B petitions to meet the congressionally mandated cap of 85,000 new H-1B filings for fiscal year 2027. The cap includes the standard 65,000 regular allocations and the 20,000 slots reserved for holders of U.S. advanced degrees, commonly known as the master's cap.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=8b_OyU8rOFI

The announcement means USCIS will not conduct a second lottery this fiscal year. In prior years, supplemental selection rounds were held when initial filings fell short of the annual cap. This year, employers had until June 30, 2026, to submit petitions for selected beneficiaries, and USCIS confirmed it received a sufficient number to fill the quota entirely.

Wage-Weighted Selection Changes the Calculus

FY2027 marked the first year USCIS replaced the traditional random lottery with a wage-based selection system. Under the new approach, registrations tied to higher Department of Labor prevailing wage levels receive priority when filings exceed the cap.

The shift produced measurable changes. Total unique beneficiary registrations dropped to approximately 211,600, down 38.5% from 336,153 submissions in the FY2026 cycle, according to data compiled by immigration law firm WR Immigration. Among those selected, 71.5% held U.S. advanced degrees, up from 57% the prior year. Only 17.7% of selected registrations fell in the lowest prevailing wage category (OEWS Level 1).

"The weighted selection system has fundamentally changed H-1B planning."

— Bernard P. Wolfsdorf, WR Immigration

The data suggests that entry-level positions and early-career workers — categories that disproportionately include recent Indian graduates on OPT — faced significantly worse odds under the new framework. USCIS has not yet published complete FY2027 selection statistics but is expected to release additional data in coming weeks.

What This Means for Indian Workers

Indians have historically been the largest group of H-1B beneficiaries, and the cap closure carries particular weight for the diaspora. Workers whose registrations were not selected will see their status in the myUSCIS portal updated to "Not Selected — Not eligible to file an H-1B cap petition based on this registration." These registrations expire with the FY2027 cap season and cannot be carried forward into FY2028.

The next opportunity for cap-subject H-1B sponsorship opens with the FY2028 registration period, expected in March 2027. Until then, affected workers and their employers must evaluate alternative pathways.

Alternatives Still on the Table

Immigration attorneys are urging employers to act quickly. Cap-exempt H-1B positions — through qualifying universities, nonprofit research organizations, and government research institutions — remain available year-round and are not subject to the annual cap.

Other options include O-1 visas for individuals with extraordinary ability, L-1 intracompany transferee visas for multinational employers, TN status for eligible Canadian and Mexican professionals, and E-3 visas for Australian nationals. For many skilled professionals already in the green card pipeline, attorneys say accelerating permanent residence applications through EB-1, EB-2 National Interest Waiver, or PERM-based sponsorship may be a more reliable long-term strategy than depending on annual lottery cycles.

"Reliance on a single immigration category is increasingly risky," Wolfsdorf wrote in a client advisory, noting that leading employers are developing diversified immigration strategies combining multiple visa categories with permanent residence planning.

Planning for FY2028

With the wage-weighted system now established, employers face a fundamentally different strategic landscape. Firms that previously filed registrations at lower wage levels may need to reassess compensation structures or identify candidates who qualify at higher tiers. Greenspoon Marder attorneys Patricia Gannon and Marcela Bermudez noted that USCIS continues to use a beneficiary-centric registration model, allowing only one registration per foreign worker to reduce duplicate entries.

Selected FY2027 beneficiaries whose petitions are approved may begin H-1B employment on October 1, 2026. For the thousands who were not selected, the wait — and the strategic recalibration — begins now.
